title: EU Climate & Energy Daily Briefing
subtitle: Sunday, 1 November 2026 — Key developments from the last 24 hours

highlights.headline: Germany's search for a nuclear waste site
highlights.summary: Finland has become the first country with a final storage facility for nuclear waste. Germany is still searching for a site, while some countries have yet to start. Costs are expected to total many billions of euros.

highlights.headline: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
highlights.summary: Defeat for Serbia's Aleksandar Vučiċ in last weekend's vote was a carbon copy of Viktor Orbán's fall in Hungary.

items.title: Bolivia declares emergency as El Nino intensifies, threatens severe weather
items.description: President Rodrigo Paz warned of severe droughts and flooding as El Nino intensifies, with at least 78,000 families already affected by drought.

items.title: 'Fascinating' rare beetle found in Wales again after 60 years
items.description: It was feared The Short-Necked Oil Beetle had become extinct in Wales after recent surveys

items.title: Spill from vandalised home oil tank kills 13 birds
items.description: A number of birds are also injured after the spill from the oil tank earlier this week.

items.title: Oil tank vandalism results in waterfowl park 'nightmare'

items.title: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
items.description: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

items.title: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
items.description: More than 320,000 people demonstrated across France against the rising cost of living and poor public services, with clashes between some protesters and police.
